t: Thomas Peterffy on market integrity after GameStop · CNBC
ot: Interactive Brokers chairman: Worried about integrity of the market
why: Cited in GameStop threads as the broker chairman saying openly that trading limits protected the system and market makers.

mentions.x: That's not a counter point. The IB Chairman explicitly said they put in the restrictions to protect market makers rather than their customers: [video]
Robinhood didn't pull the plug. Tastyworks did the same and they said they were more or less forced by Apex Clearing. Here is CEO of interactive brokers also admitting to the reasons: [video]
Have you seen the CNBC interview [1] with IBKR chairman, basically saying "once the stock goes back to the price we want we'll let retail investor trade it again"? [1] [video]
…process. Brokers were liable to cover if clearing houses do not[0]. But that is Robinhood's liquidity issue and not does justify Robinhood disabling cash accounts from buying stocks. [0] [video]
Much better quality but shorter length: [video] (uploaded by CNBC, so might get deleted someday)
…retail apps in Europe. I think the other brokers did the same. If you listen to this guy it's pretty clear he'a protecting the hedge funds. "If our customers loose money we have to put ours" [video]

…just a risk management issue and no collusion but in practice and in essence as well this was just a way to save the hedge funds(the client)'s money and ripoff the retailers(the product). [0] [video]

…a few weeks ago I won't lie, but when GME was at 325 a share and literally many thousands of people on WSB were insisting it would go to $1000. Interactive Brokers CEO confirmed this on CNBC. [video]
